name: Biang Biang Noodles

ingredients.name: neutral oil for dough and topping

steps: Mix the flour with 6 g salt and the measured 210 ml water. Knead 8–10 minutes into a smooth, firm dough; cover and rest 20 minutes. Knead briefly again, divide into eight pieces and shape short flat logs. Brush with 20 ml of the oil, cover and rest another 40 minutes so the dough stretches without tearing.

Mix soy sauce, black vinegar and sugar. Wash bok choy and prepare bowls with equal amounts of chopped garlic, spring onion, chili flakes, Sichuan pepper and sesame seeds. Keep the remaining 50 ml oil ready for heating.

Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil. Take one rested dough log, flatten it, press a line down its centre with a chopstick, then hold both ends and gently stretch into a long broad ribbon, slapping it lightly on the counter. Tear along the centre line to make two long strands. Repeat with the remaining logs.

Drop ribbons into boiling water in batches and stir gently. Cook 2–3 minutes after they float, until springy and cooked through. Lift into four warm bowls. Blanch bok choy in the same water for 1–2 minutes and add it beside the noodles.

Pour the soy-vinegar mixture over the bowls. Heat the remaining 50 ml oil until shimmering, then carefully spoon it over the garlic, chili flakes and scallions to sizzle them without burning. Toss the broad noodles through the seasoned oil and serve immediately.
tips: Stretch only well-rested dough; if it resists, cover it for 10 more minutes. Pour the hot oil away from your face. The reviewed photo shows broad folded hand-pulled ribbons with chili oil, garlic, scallions and bok choy.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
